newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares bound for more glory.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares bound for more glory.

text.p: Belgian shares, which notched up nearly two percent on Tuesday, were expected to power ahead further this week, helped by a strong dollar and Wall Street's gains, dealers and analysts said.
The Bel-20 ended 1.82 percent higher at 2,539.52 and was expected to challenge the 2,600-mark soon.
"All it takes is one good day," analyst Luc Van der Elst at Generale Bank said.
He added the market could add another 10 to 15 percent by the end of 1997 if current market conditions stayed favourable.
Van der Elst said most of the neighbouring markets had outperformed Brussels on Tuesday.
"The others bourses advanced even more, but unlike them, we did not weaken yesterday."
Brussels was closed on Monday for Belgium's National Day.
Tuesday's Bel-20 gains wiped out Friday's 1.8 percent fall completely.
Van der Elst said the Bel-20 was bolstered by the recovery of index heavyweight UCB, which ended 7.9 percent higher at 142,800, having lost nearly 11 percent on Friday.

Van der Elst said UCB continued to be lifted mainly by foreign and domestic buying interest on the back of higher profit forecasts, sales hopes for its anti-allergy drug Zyrtec in Japan and the U.S. and the share's modest liquidity.
"There are nothing but positive elements. The only danger seems to be that its weight (in the Bel-20) could be reduced," he said.
Some dealers said UCB might reach 190,000 to 200,000 francs by the end of this year. "But just as easily (it could reach) 100,000," said Patricia Decolvenaer at brokerage De Maertelaere.
Analysts said UCB, which releases first-half 1997 results on July 30, might face more hiccups if it continued to rise.
"At some stage some people will always get scared and take profits," one said.
But he added a 10 percent fall like last Friday's was fairly meaningless as UCB had already risen 48 percent in just two months. It had closed at 96,800 francs on May 22.
